narrative.overview:
T-Store should feel like a well-lit electronics counter: a clean white surface where each product sits on its own pale plinth, the price is printed plainly beside it, and the one jade thing in reach is the button you press to buy. Jade is the store's voice; white is the room it speaks in.

It is a clean, premium, easy storefront: the category standard done with full craft. Products and prices lead. Brand lives in precise details: tight display tracking, tabular prices, hairline structure, a jade that only appears where the shopper acts or has chosen, and the gold crest. Surfaces are gently layered, so cards rest a few millimetres above the counter rather than being printed on it.

Most shoppers are on phones in daylight, often switching to their banking app to pay, so light mode is the default and every pattern has to work with one thumb. Dark mode mirrors the same roles on a deep green-black.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, pale jade-grey plinths under every product photo.
Counter Jade for actions, selection and positive news; never for decoration.
Near-black ink for all reading text.
Soft resting shadows on cards; stronger lift on hover, menus and drawers.
Khmer gets its own face and taller line height.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Jade is the only green in the system. Success and positive status use Counter Jade itself, so a "Save $20" never sits beside a button in a slightly different green.

rules.name: The Jade Marks Intent Rule
rules.body: Jade appears only where the shopper can act, has chosen, or has received good news. Headlines, borders, icons at rest, and backgrounds stay neutral. If removing the jade from an element changes nothing about what the shopper can do or knows, it should not be jade.

rules.name: The Gold Is a Line Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only as the crest and as thin accent lines (underlines, rules). Never as a fill behind text, never as text, never on a button.

rules.name: The Khmer Room Rule
rules.body: Khmer text gets line height 1.8 for body and 1.45 for headings, letter spacing 0, and no truncation that could cut a cluster in half. Every layout is checked in both languages before it ships.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Any number a shopper compares (price, quantity, total, stock count) uses tabular figures so columns line up.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: On phones, the primary action of a screen is reachable at the bottom: the bottom nav, a sticky add-to-cart bar, or a checkout button that stays in view.

rules.name: The Three Heights Rule
rules.body: There are exactly three heights (Rest, Lift and Float). A new component picks one of them; it never invents a fourth shadow.

dos: **Do** use Counter Jade for the one main action in each region, and for selected and positive states.
**Do** keep all reading text in Ink, Ink Secondary or Ink Muted, never in jade.
**Do** put every product photo on a Plinth well, uncropped, with about 9% padding.
**Do** give cards the Rest shadow and lift them to Lift on hover.
**Do** set prices in tabular figures through `formatUSD()`.
**Do** check every layout in Khmer and English, light and dark, at 375px and desktop widths.
**Do** render whatever logo, site name and hero copy the admin has configured, at any length.
donts: **Don't** use gradient text, glassmorphism, floating blur blobs, pulsing pill labels or neon glows.
**Don't** add a second green, or any decorative color. If a color isn't a product photo, a status, jade intent or the crest, it's a neutral.
**Don't** use Crest Gold for text, prices, buttons or fills; it is for the crest and thin accent lines only.
**Don't** use Angkor, temple or other "cultural/touristy" ornament.
**Don't** propose themed or conceptual worlds (receipt, street map, calendar, collage) unless the user asks.
**Don't** invent a fourth shadow height or a glow.
